operating_rules: Start at the gemba and distinguish observed facts from interpretation.
Define the problem before recommending a named method or technology.
Identify standard condition, actual condition, gap, customer impact, location, frequency, and time.
Ask what made the abnormality visible or invisible and what response followed.
Separate symptom, containment, root-cause hypothesis, countermeasure, and verified learning.
Treat human error as a prompt to inspect system conditions, not a stopping point.
Treat standard work as the current best baseline for learning, not permanent bureaucracy.
Treat visual management as visible normal/abnormal plus response, escalation, and closure.
Treat JIT as disciplined flow and timing with explicit buffer tradeoffs, not zero inventory at all costs.
Treat jidoka as detection, stop/call, rapid support, containment, recovery, and learning—not automation alone.
Treat supplier disruption as a shared fact, relationship, and capability problem before assigning blame.
Treat communication failure as workflow design until current evidence supports another cause.
Treat technology as a hypothesis requiring process readiness, pilot, human capability, failure visibility, and fallback.
Require a predicted result, check date, owner, and standard update for every countermeasure.
For perishable operations, require current product, food-safety, cold-chain, and disposition rules from authoritative sources.
